Free / First course

No-limit Texas hold’em / For beginners

Poker Foundations.

Learn to follow a hand and explain your next decision. Begin with the cards, then connect the action, the board and the reasons behind a bet.

Format
Six core lessons + starter practice
Pace
One small task per visit
Access
Free, no account needed

Your route through the course

  1. Cards, actions and the pot

    Name your legal actions, count an additional call and build the best five cards.

  2. Your starting hand in context

    Describe position and earlier action before judging two private cards.

  3. Your first decisions after the flop

    Name a made hand and a draw separately, then read the action.

  4. The turn, river and showdown

    Rebuild the best five after each new card and distinguish a call price from a reason to call.

  5. Your first range

    Separate known cards, possible opposing hands and assumptions about their frequency.

  6. Betting with a purpose

    Say which worse hands might call or better hands might fold, and compare betting with checking.

Each lesson has a short first pass, a question to explain and a practice situation with a repair link. The card builder, guided hand and betting rehearsal are there when you need them.

Read / In depth

Read in depth.

Use these as references alongside the free course or for deeper study. You can start learning without reading a long essay first. Times below estimate reading, before practice or note-taking.

Complete introduction

No-limit Hold’em: rules, decisions and long-term thinking

A complete reference for rules, a counted hand, prices and ranges. Use alongside the free course or read in sections.

About 49 min read

Live cash and tournament decisions

Limped and multiway pots: how to think through live poker

Several callers, different effective stacks and a counted live hand. Cash and tournament assumptions stay explicit.

About 15 min read

10–20 BB tournament study

Short stacks beyond the chart

Available actions, antes and chip value versus prize value. Includes a checked ICM example and a review sheet.

About 15 min read

Advanced essay

Poker under uncertainty: probability, inference and decisions

Probability, Bayesian ranges, expected value and variance. Read after the basics; calculations can be reproduced.

About 50 min read

Browse every on-site guide or choose a worksheet or practice exercise.
